record.paper_title: Open Problems in the Function Theory of the Bergman Space
record.original_question: For f and g in L2_a(D), suppose f ≺ g and g ≺ f, where f ≺ g denotes the Bergman domination relation ||fh||_L2 ≤ ||gh||_L2 for all bounded analytic h. Must f equal gamma g for some unimodular constant gamma? Does the same conclusion hold under the additional assumption that f and g are bounded functions?

evidence.quote: Problem 7.2. Suppose f, g ∈ L2_a(D) have f ≺ g and g ≺ f. Must then f = gamma g for a unimodular constant gamma? What if f and g are bounded functions?
Kehe Zhu has informed me that the answer to Problem 7.2 is affirmative, and in fact a simple consequence of a property of the Berezin transform.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disk and let $dA$ be normalized area measure on $\mathbb{D}$. The Bergman space $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ is the Hilbert space of holomorphic functions $f:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ with $\|f\|_{L^2}^2=\int_{\mathbb{D}}|f(z)|^2\,dA(z)<\infty$. For $f,g\in L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$, write $f\prec g$ if\n$$\|fh\|_{L^2}\;\le\;\|gh\|_{L^2}\qquad\text{for every bounded analytic function } h:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}.$$\nSuppose $f,g\in L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ satisfy both $f\prec g$ and $g\prec f$. Must there exist a unimodular constant $\gamma\in\mathbb{C}$ (i.e. $|\gamma|=1$) such that $f=\gamma g$? Does the same conclusion hold under the additional assumption that $f$ and $g$ are bounded on $\mathbb{D}$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem has been reported as solved affirmatively by Kehe Zhu, as a consequence of a property of the Berezin transform. Both $f\prec g$ and $g\prec f$ force $f=\gamma g$ for some unimodular constant $\gamma$.
